THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
Petitioner is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner- accused husband subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both, mentally and physically and also demanded to bring money from the parental home.
3. The parties are present before this Court and they have filed the joint affidavit stating that they have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves.
The joint affidavit is placed on record.

4. Perusal of the joint affidavit indicated that the respondent No.2 herein had filed a petition under Section 13(1) (i-a) (i-b) for dissolving her marriage with the petitioner- accused No.1 on the ground of cruelty.
The matter was NC: 2023:KHC:40236 referred to the Mediation Center, Bengaluru to explore the possibility of amicable settlement between the parties.
The parties before the Mediation have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves and in terms of the settlement, the marriage has been dissolved mutually.
The accused No.1 has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.1.50 Lakh towards permanent alimony.

sentences.text: The petitioner-accused No.1 has handed over demand draft for a sum of Rs.1.50 Lakh to the respondent No.2 who is present before this Court, the receipt of which is duly acknowledged subject to realization.
The respondent No.2 has stated that she has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings against the petitioner.

6. Though the offences alleged against the petitioner is cognizable and non-compoundable, however,
having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the defacto-complainant having no objections for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioner is subjected to trial, since the probability of his conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.
